text:
maria: Quick RFC — proposal to add a per-org 'grace period' + explicit concurrency window in the API rate limiter. Goal: let short latency-sensitive bursts through without immediate 429s, but still protect overall capacity. Draft config attached below. Thoughts?

aj: Do we mean 'burst credits' or an actual queue? How is this different from current token-bucket with burst size?

maria: Good q. Current token-bucket lets X tokens accumulate and then drains; it still returns 429s immediately when tokens are gone. Proposal is hybrid: keep token-bucket but when a request would 429, if current concurrency for org < concurrency_window and queue < soft_queue_limit, we enqueue for up to grace_period_ms. If it still can't start, we return 429. So short spikes are absorbed by a tiny FIFO window.

devin: Concern: this adds tail latency and more state. Any enqueued request still consumes worker slots when it runs. We should limit this to routes that are latency-sensitive (chat/generation) and skip for embeddings/bulk. Also need metrics for queued_duration and queue_depth.

sarah: Also: 429 vs 503 policy. I think we should: 1) return 429 when request is rejected due to per-key/org quota or burst exhausted, 2) return 503 when the runtime signals system-wide overload (OOMs, GPU saturation) and we want clients to backoff immediately. That keeps client retry logic sensible.

zach: Edge pre-check: prefer to fail fast at the edge with 429 where possible to avoid routing/cold start costs. But the grace-queue should probably live in the region runtime (so we don't queue at edge for long). Maybe a two-phase check: edge precheck quick token check -> if borderline, forward and let regional runtime consider concurrency window.

maria: Exactly. Edge: cheap check, don't accept long queues. Concurrency window enforced in-region so we keep locality.

aj: How big should the window and grace period be? numbers?

maria: Draft numbers: concurrency_window=8 (per-org concurrent active requests), soft_queue_limit=16, grace_period_ms=200 (default). Burst credits still exist (refill slower). Defaults are conservative and per-org-configurable via console for enterprise.

devin: Can we make grace_period configurable per-route? E.g., chat route gets 200ms, streaming embeddings 0ms.

maria: Yes. Plan is per-route override in the rate-limiter rule.

sarah: Metrics we need for console and rollout: rate_limit.rejections{reason="hard_quota"|"concurrency"|"system_overload"}, queue.depth, queue.enqueue_ms percentiles, avg_wait_ms, p99_latency_with_queue. Also add label org_id and api_key_id. This will let customers see if graceful queuing helps.

zach: UX for rollouts: feature-flag this behind a per-tenant flag. Start with internal tenants + 5% of prod traffic, watch queue_depth and p99 tail. If tail latency increases >10% for chat we rollback.

rate-limiter-bot: snapshot metrics for last 5m (simulated): tokens_used=74%, avg_queue_depth=0.8, p99_wait_ms=180

aj: Implementation gotchas: need atomicity for decrementing tokens + checking concurrency to avoid races. Also GC for stuck queued requests (client disconnect).

devin: On client disconnect: we should decrement queued_count immediately and emit disconnect metric. Also expose a header when we enqueue: X-Redwood-Queued: true; X-Redwood-Queue-Wait-MS: <ms> so SDKs can surface this.

sarah: Good. For HTTP semantics: when we return 429 include Retry-After, and a new header X-Rate-Limit-Reason with the rejection reason. For 503 include a maintenance/retry-later message.

maria: Edge vs runtime decision summary: edge does a quick token check, region runtime enforces concurrency_window + soft queue. Return codes: 429 for quota/concurrency rejections, 503 for system overload.

aj: Suggest one more shedding strategy: prioritize requests by route and org tier. If queue full, evict lower-priority requests (bulk embeddings) before chat. That keeps UX for paying customers.

maria: Agreed. We'll add priority tiers and a pluggable eviction policy.

zach: For Dedicated tenants we may want to opt into a more permissive window or disable queueing entirely and let capacity be guaranteed. Expose that as tenant-level configuration.

maria: Next steps: I'll open an RFC PR with config schema + implementation checklist: (1) rate-limiter state machine update, (2) edge precheck change, (3) telemetry fields + console tiles, (4) feature-flag rollout plan + canary. Targeting canary next week.

devin: +1. Please include unit tests for race conditions and a load-test that simulates 1k orgs spiking.

sarah: +1 from me, will coordinate console tiles for queued metrics.

aj: :thumbsup:

zach: :rocket:
